### **Job Description and Duties**

**Please note, the Water Boards do not participate in E-Verify.**

Under the close supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist and consistent with good customer service practices and the goals of the State and Regional Water Board’s Strategic Plan, the incumbent is expected to be courteous and provide timely responses to internal/external customers, follow through on commitments, and to solicit and consider internal/external customer input when completing work assignments. This position is to work on National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System Stormwater General Permits (Permits).

Apply scientific concepts and principles about the environment, hydrology, aquatic resources, biological resources, and habitat protection in the implementation of the Permits. This may involve the following: implementation of the statewide National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System Stormwater General Permits; review and analyze stormwater data and information submitted by dischargers; lead the Stormwater Hep Desk to support and accurately respond to inquiries in a timely fashion; coordinate with the Regional Water Boards and the Office of Enforcement to prepare enforcement actions for noncompliance; and prepare effective presentation materials and make logical, comprehensible and convincing written and oral presentations at meetings as required.

Job Posting: Southern Regional EPAS Assessor

Military Department

JC-538404



Southern Regional EPAS Assessor
  
ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST

$4,551.00 - $9,787.00 per Month
  
New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

**Final Filing Date:** **11/23/2026**

### **Job Description and Duties**

The Environmental Programs Directorate supports current and future mission requirements of the California Military Department (CMD) (i.e., California Army National Guard) by assisting units, programs, and leaders to comply with environmental laws, regulations, and policy while promoting environmental stewardship at military training sites and facilities operated by the CMD.

  

Under direction of the Compliance Branch Chief or their designate, the incumbent primarily supports the Environmental Performance Assessment System (EPAS) Program, performing in-person field assessments and identifying noncompliance that have potential to cause CMD to receive notices of violation, fines, and penalties from outside regulatory agencies. Secondary duties include a broad scope of outreach and compliance assistance to Soldiers throughout California in person, via TEAMS meetings, and by telephone.

  

Requires extreme flexibility, excellent time management skills, and work within a broad range of environmental media including, but not limited to hazardous waste and materials, air quality, water quality, solid waste/recycling, storage tanks, and related environmental media. Follow up and organizational skills are essential.

  
Effective July 1, 2025, specific Bargaining Units and associated Excluded State employees are subject to a salary reduction between 2% - 4.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025) hours each month. For more details about PLP 2025, visit the California Department of Human Resources (CalHR) website.

Job Posting: Environmental Scientist

Office of Energy Infrastructure Safety

JC-537620



Environmental Scientist
  
ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST

$4,551.00 - $9,787.00 per Month
  
New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

**Final Filing Date:** **11/19/2026**

### **Job Description and Duties**

Are you looking to make a difference and join a highly motivated team working on issues critical to ensuring the safety and sustainability of California? The Office of Energy Infrastructure Safety’s Environmental Science Division is seeking a Environmental Scientist to evaluate vegetation management aspects of electric utility Wildfire Mitigation Plans (WMP).

  

The Environmental Science Division is responsible for evaluating the vegetation management aspects of utility WMPs, assessing performance in meeting vegetation management-related commitments described in the WMPs, and ensuring that each utility is reducing its risk of igniting a catastrophic wildfire. To this end, Division scientists review regulatory filings and utility procedures, analyze reported data, perform audits, conduct field inspections, publish findings, and engage with the utilities and interested parties. Division scientists serve as subject-matter experts in utility vegetation management and environmental policy related to wildfire risk reduction. Our team of scientists is highly collaborative and works closely with the Performance Assessment, Electrical Safety Policy, and Data Analytics Divisions.

Under close supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) of the Environmental Policy Branch in the Environmental Science Division, the incumbent will review and evaluate vegetation management-related aspects of electric utility Wildfire Mitigation Plans, develop utility vegetation management best management practices for wildfire safety, and contribute to the development of Guidelines. The incumbent will also develop and maintain relationships with Federal, State, and local agency partners and serve as an environmental science subject matter expert to assist other Energy Safety Divisions.

The reporting location for this position is California Natural Resources Agency Building located at 715 P Street, Sacramento, CA 95814.

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

Effective July 1, 2025, The California Department of Human Resources (CalHR) implemented the Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025). PLP 2025 directs that each employee shall receive a 3 percent reduction in pay in exchange for 5 hours PLP 2025 leave credits, monthly. The salary range(s) included in the job advertisement do not reflect the 3 percent reduction in pay.

This position is headquartered in Sacramento, California and may be eligible for a hybrid telework schedule for applicants residing in California, in accordance with Government Code Section 14200 and the Department’s current telework policy. A hybrid schedule typically includes working remotely and physically reporting to the office a minimum of four days per week; however, the specific number of in-office days and the overall telework schedule are subject to change at the sole discretion of the Department based on operational needs, policy changes, or direction from State leadership. Employees may be required to report to their designated work location with minimal notice. Telework does not alter the terms and conditions of employment, essential job functions, or compliance with departmental policies**.**

* Incumbent is required to travel, including overnight stays, and on occasion be required to work unusual hours.
* Energy Safety will utilize a Hybrid Remote/In-person approach enabling staff to telework, when approved by management.
* Energy Safety will use shared workspaces for most staff (hoteling stations) when required to work in the office.

jobs.description:
Discover your full potential. At Tetra Tech, we are collaborating with industry-leading experts for a sustainable future for our world. We combine consulting and engineering with advanced analytics and technology to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our innovation hubs across the globe will enable you to share ideas and best practices while growing your professional network. Wherever you are in your career journey, you will benefit from working with world-class engineers, scientists, and technical specialists.

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential – join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

Apply today and join the company that is Leading with Science®.

Tetra Tech is seeking a self-motivated, experienced Environmental Scientist / Compliance Specialist to lead and expand our landfill and air quality compliance services within the solid waste industry. This position is ideal for candidates with a strong technical background in air regulations, Landfill Gas (LFG) systems, emissions compliance, environmental permitting, and regulatory interpretation, who are comfortable working with limited oversight while supporting complex, multi-site compliance programs.

In this role, you will independently manage and support regulatory compliance programs by analyzing complex field and operational datasets, interpreting and applying air quality regulations and permit requirements, preparing and reviewing compliance reports, and leading air permitting and emissions calculation efforts. The primary focus areas include LFG monitoring, Surface Emissions Monitoring (SEM), Landfill Gas‑to‑Energy (LFGTE) Systems, air quality permitting, and compliance with California Landfill Methane Regulation (LMR) requirements, New Source Performance Standards (NSPS), and National Emissions Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants (NESHAP) applicable to solid waste facilities.

This position is primarily remote, with limited, as‑needed travel or occasional site visits. Candidates must be comfortable working independently, exercising professional judgment, and collaborating with project managers, field staff, engineers, clients, and regulatory specialists across geographically dispersed teams.

This position is eligible for our full benefits package including but not limited to Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, AD&D, Disability, Flexible Spending Account (FSA), Health Spending Account (HSA), My Flex Time (MFT – paid time off), 401K, and an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. The pay range for this position is $90K–$110K annually, based on qualifications, location, and experience. **Only those that attach a cover letter will be considered.** The deadline to apply is 11/11/2026.

**Your Role**:

* Independently review, analyze, interpret, and validate landfill air quality and LFG monitoring data, including wellfield data, SEM results, and air emissions datasets for multiple facilities.
* Evaluate monitoring and operational data against regulatory standards, permit conditions, and LMR, NSPS, and NESHAP requirements, identifying compliance risks, deviations, and corrective action needs.
* Prepare, review, and finalize environmental compliance reports, including air compliance summaries, annual and quarterly monitoring reports, deviation analyses, and regulatory submittals.
* Lead the development and preparation of air quality permit applications, amendments, and renewals, including emissions calculations, regulatory applicability analyses, and compliance demonstrations.
* Manage and oversee large, multi‑site datasets related to air emissions, LFG, SEM results, compliance schedules, and agency reporting deadlines.
* Develop, maintain, and refine standardized templates, tools, and compliance trackers to ensure consistent, accurate, and timely reporting across multiple facilities and clients.
* Coordinate closely with on‑site operations staff, technicians, contractors, and engineers to ensure monitoring programs, testing protocols, and system performance meet regulatory and permit requirements.
* Serve as a technical resource to Project Managers and junior staff, supporting deliverables, schedules, quality control reviews, and client coordination.
* Support client and agency interactions, including preparation for inspections, agency inquiries, and audit responses.
* Contribute to and support multidisciplinary engineering, permitting, and environmental projects, providing subject‑matter expertise in landfill and air quality compliance.

**Required Qualifications**:

* Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, or a related field.
* 5+ years of experience in environmental science, air quality, regulatory compliance, or a related technical field.
* Strong working knowledge of air quality regulations, including LMR, NSPS, NESHAP, and permit compliance applicable to landfills and solid waste facilities.
* Demonstrated experience preparing and reviewing air permits, compliance reports, emissions calculations, and regulatory submittals.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including advanced technical and regulatory writing.
* Proficiency in MS Office, specifically advanced use of Word and Excel for data analysis, tracking, and reporting.
* Proven ability to work independently in

The State Water Resources Control Board’s Division of Water Rights has an opening for an Environmental Scientist (Aquatic/Fisheries Scientist) in the Bay-Delta Section within the Bay Delta & Hearings Programs Branch. This position is located at 1001 I Street, 14th Floor, Sacramento, CA 95814, right in the heart of downtown next to light rail stations and other public transportation.

  

**Duties:**

  

Under the close supervision of the State Water Resources Control Board’s (State Water Board) Bay-Delta Sacramento Unit Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), and consistent with good customer service practices and the goals of the State and Regional Board’s Strategic Plan, the incumbent will perform complex and varied aquatic/fisheries analyses, research, and modeling assignments related to the San Francisco Bay/Sacramento-San Joaquin River Delta (Bay-Delta).

  

The incumbent will prepare scientific analyses and documentation to assist with the high priority complex technical and regulatory assignments for the Division of Water Rights and State Water Board.

  

This position is specifically focused on State Water Board regulatory and planning activities in the Bay-Delta.

  

In addition, the incumbent may review hydrologic modeling of Central Valley rivers and estuaries to investigate how water management actions may affect flows, river and reservoir temperatures, fisheries and other aquatic habitat, water quality, and water rights.
